text.0_Chapter, 0_Mishnah, 0_Paragraph: Moses. For most of the statements in this tractate, an explanation and expanded discussion can be found in the appended work אבות דר׳ נתן (Avot de-Rabbi Natan), which is printed together with all Talmud editions and is cited here as AN. ‘EM.’ refers to my essay The First Mishnah (Berlin 1882).
text.0_Chapter, 0_Mishnah, 1_Paragraph: ‘received the Torah.’ Here this refers primarily to ‘the Oral Teaching’ (תורה שבעל פה), also called מסורת (tradition = παράδοσις [of the fathers]) or קבלה (transmission = διαδοχή) (compare Josephus, Antiquities XIII, 10, 6). The ‘fathers’ who transmitted the Oral Teaching from generation to generation are the אבות (Avot), after whom this tractate is named; see EM. pp. 6 and 26.
text.0_Chapter, 0_Mishnah, 2_Paragraph: ‘from Sinai.’ מסיני literally means ‘from Sinai,’ i.e. originating from Sinai; compare Eduyot VIII, 7.
text.0_Chapter, 0_Mishnah, 3_Paragraph: ‘and transmitted it to Joshua.’ מסר is Aramaic for ‘to hand over’ or ‘to transmit’; from this comes מסורת (tradition), see note 2.
text.0_Chapter, 0_Mishnah, 4_Paragraph: ‘and Joshua to the Elders.’ See Joshua 24:31.
text.0_Chapter, 0_Mishnah, 5_Paragraph: ‘and the Elders to the Prophets.’ See Jeremiah 7:25. In AN. 1, the Judges (שופטים) are inserted between the Elders (זקנים) and the Prophets.
text.0_Chapter, 0_Mishnah, 6_Paragraph: ‘and the Prophets transmitted it to the Men of the Great Assembly.’ This was the supreme court composed of 120 men, which in the early period of the Second Temple occupied a position similar to that of the later Sanhedrin, which was likewise called כנסת (= כנישתא; see Megillat Taanit ch. 10). Compare Magazine for the Science of Judaism (1883), pp. 46–63. In AN. 1, חגי, זכריה, ומלאכי (Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi) are added between ‘the Prophets’ and ‘the Men of the Great Assembly.’
text.0_Chapter, 0_Mishnah, 8_Paragraph: ‘careful.’ מתון means slow, calm, deliberate; from it comes המתין, ‘to wait.’
text.0_Chapter, 0_Mishnah, 9_Paragraph: ‘in judgment.’ According to AN. 1, this means in every legal decision.
text.0_Chapter, 0_Mishnah, 10_Paragraph: ‘and make a fence around the Torah.’ Establish protective measures safeguarding the Law; compare the phrase חכמים עשו סייג לדבריהם — ‘the Sages made a fence around their words’ (Berakhot 4b). According to AN. 2–3, this instruction originally stood second, while ‘raise up many disciples’ stood third.
text.0_Chapter, 1_Mishnah, 0_Paragraph: “Simon the Righteous.” This refers to Simon I, son of Onias (Josephus, Antiquities XII, 2, 4), who served as High Priest around 300 BCE.
text.0_Chapter, 1_Mishnah, 1_Paragraph: “belonged to the remnant of the Great Assembly.” He was among the last members of that assembly. With him and his colleagues, the period of the אנשי כנסת הגדולה (Men of the Great Assembly) comes to an end. Their teachings and enactments were later cited as דברי סופרים (words of the scribes) or מעשה זקנים (deeds/traditions of the elders), as in Yadayim IV, 3; compare the article cited above, p. 58ff.
text.0_Chapter, 1_Mishnah, 2_Paragraph: “upon the service [of God].” עבודת בית המקדש, i.e. the Temple service (called עבורה in AN. 4).
text.0_Chapter, 1_Mishnah, 3_Paragraph: “and upon acts of lovingkindness.” Meaning personal acts of kindness and care, distinguished from צדקה, charitable giving or alms (see Sukkah 49b).
text.0_Chapter, 1_Mishnah, 4_Paragraph: The Jerusalem Talmud, Taanit IV 68a, finds these three things mentioned here alluded to in Isaiah 51:16; compare further below, Mishnah 18.
